newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish ARR opts to buy less grain at higher price.
newsitem.headline: Polish ARR opts to buy less grain at higher price.

text.p: The council of Poland's Agriculture Market Agency (ARR), the food market regulator, on Tuesday opted for a 1997 programme of higher intervention prices and a lower level of agricultural product purchases.
ARR officials said at a council meeting the programme anticipated purchases of 487,800 tonnes of wheat next year, of which 180,000 tonnes would be imported, and 52,500 tonnes of rye.
The forecast purchase price for wheat was 620 zlotys per tonne and for rye 460 zlotys.

The council rejected a proposal drafted by the government and trade unions proposing lower intervention prices and higher agricultural purchases totalling 525,000 tonnes of wheat and 63,500 tonnes of rye next year.
The Agency has carried out its plan to import 180,000 tonnes of wheat this year. The wheat was purchased in the last quarter of 1996 at 610 zlotys a tonne for delivery in the first quarter of 1997.
The ARR forecast that the sale price in 1997 of grain from 1996 reserves would be 630 zlotys per tonne for wheat and 410 zlotys for rye. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
